summary.text: Jim Baird is the Republican incumbent for Indiana's 4th District, a Vietnam War veteran, farmer and Purdue-educated animal nutritionist who served as a Putnam County commissioner and in the Indiana House before his 2018 election to Congress. He sits on the Agriculture, Science, Space, and Technology, and Foreign Affairs committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in Fountain County, Indiana, in 1945; his official biography describes him as a lifelong resident of West Central Indiana.

Earned bachelor's and master's degrees in animal science from Purdue University (1967, 1969) and, after returning from Vietnam, a doctorate in monogastric nutrition from the University of Kentucky (1975).

Served in the U.S. Army from 1969 to 1972; his official biography describes him as a decorated Vietnam War veteran awarded a Bronze Star with V device and two Purple Hearts, and says his unit was inducted into the United States Transportation Corps Hall of Fame.
Before Congress, ran a home healthcare agency and a family farm and worked as a small business owner.
Served as Putnam County commissioner from 2006 to 2010.
Served in the Indiana House of Representatives from 2010 to 2018, including on the Ways and Means Committee, according to his official biography.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2018; serves on the Committee on Agriculture (Vice Chair of the Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology subcommittee), the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and the Committee on Foreign Affairs in the 119th Congress.

Active or former member of the Rotary Club of Greencastle, the Putnam County Fair and 4-H Club Association, VFW, American Legion and Indiana Farm Bureau, and served on the advisory council for Purdue University's Dean of Agriculture; he is married to Danise and they have three children, according to his official biography.
Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 60.5% of the vote.
